title: CityGPT: Empowering Urban Spatial Cognition of Large Language Models

problem.claim: Large language models often perform poorly on real-life geospatial tasks in urban environments.

gap.claim: Their limitation is attributed to insufficient physical-world knowledge and relevant training data.

contributions.claim: CityGPT is a framework that integrates a city-scale world model into large language models to improve urban spatial understanding and task solving.
The work introduces the CityInstruction instruction-tuning dataset and the SWFT self-weighted fine-tuning method for improving urban spatial capabilities.
The work develops CityEval, a text-based spatial benchmark covering urban scenarios and geospatial tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe SWFT as a novel self-weighted fine-tuning method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that smaller language models trained with CityInstruction and SWFT perform competitively with, and sometimes better than, proprietary models on CityEval.
The authors report that the dataset, benchmark, and source code are open-sourced.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large language models have achieved notable success in language generation and reasoning across domains.
They struggle with urban geospatial tasks because of limited physical-world knowledge and relevant training data.
CityGPT addresses the gap by integrating a city-scale world model into language models.
The framework combines CityInstruction, SWFT fine-tuning, and the CityEval benchmark.
The authors report competitive benchmark performance and open-source release of the main artifacts.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines domain-specific instruction data with a fine-tuning method designed for urban spatial capabilities.

interpretation.claim: Specialized data and training procedures may help adapt general language models to domain-specific spatial reasoning.

application.claim: For another domain, construct targeted instruction data and evaluate whether a domain-aware fine-tuning procedure improves the relevant capabilities.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which component or combination is responsible for the reported improvements.

unknowns: CityInstruction dataset size, composition, and construction process
SWFT algorithmic details and training configuration
CityEval tasks, data sources, metrics, and evaluation protocol
Magnitude and statistical reliability of reported improvements
